# nexus piholeblocking stop

Stop Pi-hole blocking

Disables Pi-hole's blocking (pihole disable): DNS keeps answering, but nothing is blocked. With durationSeconds (1 to 86400), a transient systemd timer, nexus-pihole-reenable, created before blocking is disabled, re-enables it when the time elapses, even after the operation ended and across a restart of nexusd; without it, blocking stays off until start-blocking. A new stop replaces any pending re-enable with its own. Reloads Pi-hole's lists; does not restart DNS. The result is the state read back, with reenableAt. Side effects: runs pihole disable as root; with durationSeconds, creates (or replaces) the transient systemd timer nexus-pihole-reenable; reloads Pi-hole's lists. Long-running: answers 202 with an operation, queued in order behind every other Pi-hole operation (the pihole lane); it runs as root in its own systemd unit (Pi-hole needs systemd; OpenRC hosts are not supported) outside nexusd's sandbox, so it survives a restart of nexusd. A queued operation can be canceled; a running one cannot. Fails pihole-command-failed when a command fails or the read-back shows blocking still on.

## Usage

```
nexus piholeblocking stop [flags]
```

## Examples

```
  # Stop Pi-hole blocking
  nexus piholeblocking stop
  # The same, safe to retry
  nexus piholeblocking stop --idempotency-key <key>
```

## Flags

```
      --duration-seconds int     Re-enable blocking automatically after this many seconds, 1 to 86400. Absent disables blocking until start-blocking.
      --filter stringArray       key=value, repeatable: print only objects whose dot path has this value; a repeated key matches any of its values
      --follow                   stream the operation's output to stderr while waiting
  -h, --help                     help for stop
      --idempotency-key string   Idempotency-Key header: a retry with the same key and input returns the original operation (at most 255 visible ASCII characters)
      --no-wait                  print the operation as accepted and exit, without waiting for it to end
  -o, --output string            output format: table, json, jsonl, yaml (default table on a terminal, jsonl otherwise)
      --select strings           print only these dot paths of each object, comma-separated, such as name,properties.state; host and id are always kept
      --tag strings              target every configured host with this tag; comma-separated or repeated for any of several
      --timeout duration         stop waiting after this long, such as 90s or 5m, and exit 7; the operation is not canceled
      --yes                      do not ask for confirmation; required to mutate without a terminal
```

## Global flags

```
      --host string   target hosts: configured names, comma-separated, or all (default: NEXUS_HOST, then the default host)
      --verbose       log each request and response status to stderr
```
